column2: Anthropologists describe animism as the belief that rivers, rocks, and trees all possess spirits.
column3: 人類學家將泛靈信仰描述為相信河流、岩石與樹木都擁有靈魂。
column4: animism and ancestor worship (泛靈信仰與祖先崇拜)
column5: anima 是「靈魂」，animal 動物有靈，animism 就是萬物皆有靈

column2: The Roman pantheon included Jupiter, Mars, and dozens of lesser gods.
column3: 羅馬的諸神包含朱比特、瑪爾斯和數十位次要神祇。
column5: pan 全部 + theon 神：全部的神都住在同一座神殿

column2: Immigrant children often go through acculturation, adopting local customs while keeping parts of their heritage.
column3: 移民兒童常經歷文化涵化，在採納當地習俗的同時保留部分傳統。
column5: ac 朝向 + culture 文化：慢慢靠向新的文化

column2: Over several generations, assimilation led the immigrant community to adopt the main language and drop many old customs.
column3: 歷經數個世代，同化使這個移民社群採用主流語言，並放棄許多舊習俗。
column5: as + similar 相似：慢慢變得跟大家一樣

column2: Indigenous peoples of the Arctic have hunted seals for thousands of years.
column3: 北極的原住民族已獵捕海豹數千年。
column5: in 裡面 + gen 出生：在這片土地出生長大的

column2: Aboriginal rock paintings in northern Australia are among the oldest artworks on Earth.
column3: 澳洲北部的原住民岩畫是地球上最古老的藝術品之一。
column5: ab 從 + origin 起源：從最初起源就住在那裡

column2: Archaeologists dated the clay bowl, a handmade artifact, to about three thousand years ago.
column3: 考古學家將這只陶碗這件手工製品，定年在大約三千年前。
column5: art 手工 + fact 做成：人親手做出來的東西

column2: The monastery guards a relic, a scrap of cloth said to be centuries old.
column3: 修道院保管著一件遺物，據說是有數百年歷史的一小塊布。
column4: relic of the past (過去的遺物)
column5: relic 像 relax 之後留下：被時間留在後面的老東西

column2: Workers excavated the hillside to uncover the foundations of a Roman villa.
column3: 工人挖掘山坡，以找出一座羅馬別墅的地基。
column5: ex 向外 + cave 洞：挖個洞把土運出來

column2: The excavation lasted six summers and revealed an entire marketplace beneath the farmland.
column3: 這次發掘持續了六個夏天，在農田底下挖出整座市集。
column5: excavate 挖洞加 tion 變名詞：挖出來的工程
column8: 考古發掘作業；發掘工地

column2: Greek theaters from antiquity still host performances because of their remarkable acoustics.
column3: 古代的希臘劇場因音響效果出色，至今仍舉辦演出。
column5: antiquity 和 antique 古董同家族，都是很久以前

column2: Tourists walked among the ruins of the temple, where only a few columns still stood.
column3: 遊客在神殿的廢墟間漫步，那裡只剩幾根石柱仍然矗立。
column5: ruin 是毀壞，ruins 是毀壞後剩下的一堆石頭

column2: The city built a white marble monument to honor the soldiers who defended the bridge.
column3: 市政府建了一座白色大理石紀念碑，以紀念守衛這座橋的士兵。
column5: mon 提醒 + ument：立起來提醒大家別忘記

column2: Scholars could read Egyptian hieroglyphics only after the Rosetta Stone showed the same text in three scripts.
column3: 直到羅塞塔石碑以三種文字呈現相同內容，學者才讀懂古埃及象形文字。
column5: hiero 神聖 + glyph 雕刻：神廟牆上刻的神聖符號

column2: Sumerian scribes pressed a reed into wet clay to write cuneiform, one of the earliest writing systems.
column3: 蘇美的書記員把蘆葦桿壓進濕黏土來書寫楔形文字，這是最早的書寫系統之一。
column5: cune 楔子 + form 形狀：字痕像一顆顆小楔子

column2: The cave wall bears a pictograph of a deer, drawn to show what hunters hoped to find.
column3: 洞穴牆壁上有一幅鹿的象形圖畫，描繪獵人希望找到的獵物。
column5: picture 圖畫 + graph 書寫：用圖畫來寫字

column2: In phonology class, students learned why English speakers hear "pat" and "bat" as different words.
column3: 在音韻學課堂上，學生學到為什麼說英語的人會把 pat 和 bat 聽成不同的字。
column5: phone 聲音 + logy 學問：像 telephone 電話的聲音

column2: In English syntax, adjectives usually come before the nouns they describe.
column3: 在英語句法中，形容詞通常放在所描述的名詞之前。
column5: syn 一起 + tax 排列：把字排在一起成句子

column2: Semantics explains why "cheap" and "inexpensive" mean nearly the same thing yet sound different to buyers.
column3: 語意學解釋了為什麼「cheap」與「inexpensive」意思幾乎相同，卻讓買家感受不同。
column5: sem 像 sign 記號：研究記號背後的意思

column2: Pragmatics helps explain why "Can you pass the salt?" is a request, not a question about ability.
column3: 語用學能解釋為什麼「你能把鹽遞過來嗎？」是請求，而不是在問能力。
column5: pragma 行動，像 practical 實用：看話語在場合中做了什麼
column8: 語用學；語境中的話語應用

column2: People from the northern valley speak a dialect whose vowels sound unfamiliar to city residents.
column3: 北部山谷的人說一種方言，其母音對城市居民來說聽起來很陌生。
column5: dia 之間 + lect 說：同一語言裡各地不同的說法

column2: English serves as a lingua franca at international science conferences, where speakers share no other language.
column3: 英語是國際科學研討會上的通用語，因為與會者沒有其他共同語言。
column5: lingua 像 language 語言，franca 是共通：大家都能溝通

column2: Traders created a pidgin, a simplified blend of two languages, to bargain at the harbor.
column3: 商人創造了一種洋涇浜，也就是兩種語言簡化後的混合，用來在港口討價還價。
column5: pidgin 唸起來像 pigeon 鴿子：簡單的咕咕話也能做生意
column8: 洋涇浜；混雜的商務接觸語

column2: Children who grew up hearing a pidgin turned it into a creole with fixed grammar.
column3: 從小聽洋涇浜長大的孩子，把它發展成語法固定的克里奧爾語。
column5: creole 像 create 創造：孩子創造出來的新母語
column8: 克里奧爾語；母語化的混合語

column2: Our bilingual teacher explains each science lesson in both English and Mandarin.
column3: 我們的雙語老師用英語和華語講解每一堂自然課。
column5: bi 二 + lingual 語言：bicycle 兩輪，bilingual 兩語

column2: Monolingual speakers of English can struggle in places where few people understand the language.
column3: 只會單一語言的英語使用者，在很少人懂英語的地方可能會很吃力。
column5: mono 單一 + lingual 語言：像 monorail 單軌

column2: Freud used the word neurosis for long-lasting anxiety that disturbs daily life without breaking contact with reality.
column3: 佛洛伊德用「精神官能症」一詞，指干擾日常生活但沒有脫離現實的長期焦慮。
column4: suffer from neurosis (罹患精神官能症)
column5: neuro 神經 + sis 病狀：神經緊繃過頭的毛病

column2: Unlike neurosis, psychosis involves a break with reality, and patients may see or hear things that are not there.
column3: 與官能症不同，精神病性障礙會脫離現實，患者可能看到或聽到不存在的事物。
column5: psycho 心靈 + sis 病：心靈整個離開了現實

column2: The patient's hallucination was so vivid that she insisted she could hear music in the silent room.
column3: 病患的幻覺非常逼真，她堅稱自己在安靜的房間裡聽得到音樂。
column5: 哈路西內申：明明沒有東西，卻「哈」地看到了

column2: He lived under the delusion that he was a famous inventor, though he had never built anything.
column3: 他活在自己是知名發明家的妄想中，儘管他從未造出任何東西。
column5: de 向下 + lude 玩弄：被自己的想法騙了還深信不疑
column8: 妄想；堅信不移的錯誤想法

column2: After the accident, he had amnesia and could not remember his own address.
column3: 意外之後他罹患失憶症，連自己的住址都想不起來。
column5: a 無 + mnes 記憶：沒有記憶，像 mnemonic 記憶術

column2: After the stroke, aphasia left the former teacher unable to find the words she wanted.
column3: 中風之後，失語症讓這位前教師無法找到她想說的字詞。
column5: a 無 + phasia 言語：失去說話的能力

column2: Her grandfather's dementia slowly erased his memory of familiar faces and places.
column3: 她祖父的失智症慢慢抹去他對熟悉面孔與地方的記憶。
column5: de 離開 + ment 心智：心智一點一點離開

column2: Her phobia of heights made even a second-floor balcony feel terrifying.
column3: 她的懼高症讓她連二樓陽台都覺得很可怕。
column4: phobia of spiders (對蜘蛛的恐懼症)
column5: phobia 諧音「佛比啊」：一看到就大喊「佛啊」想躲開
column8: 對特定對象的極度恐懼症

column2: Years after the flood, the villagers still carried the trauma of losing their homes.
column3: 洪水過後多年，村民仍背負著失去家園的心理創傷。
column5: 想像心裡被重重撞出一塊大瘀青，久久不消

column2: After weeping through the tragic play, the audience felt a catharsis, as if their tension had been washed away.
column3: 看完悲劇哭了一場後，觀眾感到情緒宣洩，彷彿緊張都被沖走了。
column5: cathar 是乾淨：哭完像洗過澡，心裡變乾淨了

column2: Freud described sublimation as turning an unacceptable urge, such as anger, into a productive activity like painting.
column3: 佛洛伊德把昇華描述為將不被接受的衝動，例如憤怒，轉為像繪畫這類有益的活動。
column5: 和 sublime 崇高同家族：把壞情緒提升成美好的事
column8: 昇華；將本能轉化的防衛機制

column2: As an introvert, Mia recharges by reading alone after a long day of group projects.
column3: 身為內向者，米雅在一整天的小組專題後，靠獨自閱讀來恢復精力。
column5: intro 向內 + vert 轉：往內轉的人

column2: An extrovert like Leo gets energy from meeting new people at parties.
column3: 像里歐這樣的外向者，會從派對上認識新朋友的過程中獲得活力。
column5: extro 向外 + vert 轉：往外轉向人群的人

column2: A good nurse shows empathy by imagining how frightened the patient must feel.
column3: 好護理師會設想病患有多害怕，藉此表現同理心。
column5: em 進入 + path 感受：走進別人的感受裡
column8: 同理心；感同身受的能力
